source.text: Λέγω δέ, ἐφ’ ὅσον χρόνον ὁ κληρονόμος νήπιός ἐστιν, οὐδὲν διαφέρει δούλου κύριος πάντων ὤν, ἀλλὰ ὑπὸ ἐπιτρόπους ἐστὶ καὶ οἰκονόμους ἄχρι τῆς προθεσμίας τοῦ πατρός.

records.literal_gloss: I say now, for as much time [as] the heir a child is, nothing he differs from a slave, lord of all being, \v 2 but under guardians he is and managers until the set-beforehand [time] of the father.

en.L: Now I say, for as long a time as the heir is a child, he differs in nothing from a slave, though he is lord of all, \v 2 but he is under guardians and managers until the time set beforehand by the father.
en.B: Here is what I mean. While the heir is still a child, his position is no better than a slave's, even though he is master of everything. \v 2 Guardians and managers have charge of him until the date his father has set.
en.R: Think of it like this. A child who will inherit everything his father owns is no better off than a slave while he is still young, even though it all belongs to him. \v 2 Other people are put in charge of him and of his property until the time his father has chosen.

es.L: Ahora digo: durante todo el tiempo que el heredero es niño, no se diferencia en nada de un esclavo, aunque es dueño de todo, \v 2 sino que está bajo tutores y administradores hasta el tiempo fijado de antemano por el padre.
es.B: Me explico: mientras el heredero es todavía menor de edad, su situación no es mejor que la de un esclavo, aunque es dueño de todo. \v 2 Tutores y administradores están a cargo de él hasta la fecha que su padre ha fijado.
es.R: Pongamos un ejemplo. Un niño que va a heredar todo lo que tiene su padre no está mejor que un esclavo mientras es pequeño, aunque todo le pertenece. \v 2 Otras personas se encargan de él y de sus bienes hasta el momento que su padre ha escogido.

sw.L: Basi nasema, kwa muda wote ambao mrithi ni mtoto, hatofautiani na mtumwa kwa lolote, ingawa ni bwana wa vyote, \v 2 bali yuko chini ya wasimamizi na mawakili mpaka wakati uliowekwa mapema na baba.
sw.B: Ninamaanisha hivi: maadamu mrithi bado ni mtoto mdogo, hali yake si bora kuliko ya mtumwa, ingawa ndiye mwenye mali yote. \v 2 Wasimamizi na mawakili wana mamlaka juu yake mpaka siku ambayo baba yake ameiweka.
sw.R: Fikirini mfano huu. Mtoto atakayerithi kila kitu alicho nacho baba yake si bora kuliko mtumwa wakati bado ni mdogo, ingawa vitu vyote ni mali yake. \v 2 Watu wengine wamewekwa kumsimamia yeye na mali yake mpaka wakati ambao baba yake ameuchagua.

fr.L: Or je dis : aussi longtemps que l’héritier est un enfant, il ne diffère en rien d’un esclave, bien qu’il soit maître de tout, \v 2 mais il est sous des tuteurs et des intendants jusqu’au moment fixé d’avance par le père.
fr.B: Voici ce que je veux dire. Tant que l’héritier est encore mineur, sa situation n’est en rien meilleure que celle d’un esclave, bien qu’il soit le maître de tout. \v 2 Des tuteurs et des intendants ont autorité sur lui jusqu’à la date que son père a fixée.
fr.R: Pensez-y de cette façon. Un enfant qui héritera de tout ce que possède son père n’est pas mieux loti qu’un esclave tant qu’il est jeune, même si tout lui appartient. \v 2 D’autres personnes sont chargées de s’occuper de lui et de ses biens jusqu’au moment que son père a choisi.

ko.L: 내가 말합니다. 상속자가 어린아이로 있는 동안에는, 그가 모든 것의 주인이라도 노예와 조금도 다르지 않고, \v 2 아버지가 미리 정한 때까지 후견인들과 관리인들 아래 있습니다.
ko.B: 내 말은 이것입니다. 상속자가 아직 어린아이일 때에는, 그가 모든 것의 주인이라 해도 노예보다 나을 것이 없습니다. \v 2 아버지가 정해 둔 날까지는 후견인들과 관리인들이 그를 맡아 돌봅니다.
ko.R: 이렇게 생각해 보십시오. 아버지의 모든 재산을 물려받을 아이라도, 아직 어릴 때에는 노예보다 나을 것이 없습니다. 모든 것이 다 그의 것인데도 그렇습니다. \v 2 아버지가 정해 둔 때가 될 때까지는 다른 사람들이 그 아이와 그의 재산을 맡아 관리합니다.

vi.L: Tôi nói rằng, bao lâu người thừa kế còn là trẻ nhỏ, thì người ấy chẳng khác gì một nô lệ, dù là chủ của mọi sự, \v 2 nhưng ở dưới quyền những người giám hộ và những người quản lý cho đến thời điểm người cha đã định trước.
vi.B: Ý tôi là thế này: bao lâu người thừa kế còn là trẻ nhỏ, thì địa vị của người ấy chẳng hơn gì một nô lệ, dù người ấy là chủ của mọi sự. \v 2 Người ấy ở dưới quyền những người giám hộ và quản lý cho đến ngày người cha đã định.
vi.R: Hãy nghĩ như thế này. Một đứa trẻ sẽ thừa hưởng mọi thứ cha mình có, nhưng khi còn nhỏ thì nó chẳng hơn gì một nô lệ, dù mọi thứ ấy đều thuộc về nó. \v 2 Có những người khác được giao trông coi nó và tài sản của nó cho đến thời điểm cha nó đã chọn.

pt.L: Digo, porém: durante todo o tempo em que o herdeiro é menor, em nada difere de um escravo, embora seja senhor de tudo, \v 2 mas está debaixo de tutores e administradores até o tempo marcado de antemão pelo pai.
pt.B: O que quero dizer é isto: enquanto o herdeiro ainda é criança, a situação dele não é melhor que a de um escravo, embora ele seja dono de tudo. \v 2 Tutores e administradores cuidam dele até a data que o pai marcou.
pt.R: Pensem assim: um menino que vai herdar tudo o que o pai tem não está em situação melhor que um escravo enquanto ainda é pequeno, embora tudo pertença a ele. \v 2 Outras pessoas são encarregadas dele e dos seus bens até o tempo que o pai escolheu.

am.L: እላለሁም፤ ወራሹ ሕፃን በሆነበት ጊዜ ሁሉ፣ የሁሉ ጌታ ቢሆንም ከባሪያ በምንም አይለይም፤ \v 2 ነገር ግን አባቱ አስቀድሞ እስከ ወሰነው ጊዜ ድረስ ከአሳዳጊዎችና ከመጋቢዎች በታች ነው።
am.B: ማለቴ ይህ ነው፤ ወራሹ ገና ሕፃን ሳለ፣ የሁሉ ነገር ጌታ ቢሆንም እንኳ፣ አቋሙ ከባሪያ የተሻለ አይደለም። \v 2 አባቱ እስከ ወሰነው ቀን ድረስ አሳዳጊዎችና መጋቢዎች ይቆጣጠሩታል።
am.R: እንዲህ ብላችሁ አስቡ። አባቱ ያለውን ሁሉ የሚወርስ ልጅ ገና ትንሽ ሳለ፣ ሁሉም የእርሱ ቢሆንም እንኳ፣ ከባሪያ የተሻለ ነገር የለውም። \v 2 አባቱ እስከ መረጠው ጊዜ ድረስ ሌሎች ሰዎች በእርሱና በንብረቱ ላይ ኃላፊዎች ይሆናሉ።

decisions.choice: a child under age: a minor, not yet legally able to act for himself
decisions.reason: νήπιος can mean a baby, but here it stands against the grown heir who takes control of the estate. The point is legal standing, not age in years: until the set time the heir cannot manage what is his.

decisions.choice: though he is owner of everything: owner by right, not yet in practice
alternatives: he is already in control of the estate
decisions.reason: The participle is concessive. The estate already belongs to the heir, yet while he is under age he has no more say over it than a slave of the household.

decisions.choice: guardians and managers: those who had charge of a minor and of his property
decisions.reason: An ἐπίτροπος was a guardian appointed for a child, and an οἰκονόμος was a steward who ran property or a household. Greek and Roman law both made such arrangements for heirs who were under age. Paul uses the two words together for the people who had charge over the child and over what he would inherit.

decisions.choice: the date set in advance by the father
decisions.reason: προθεσμία is a time fixed beforehand. Paul's picture does not fit any one legal system exactly, and it does not say whether the father is living or dead. What matters for his argument is that the father decides when the heir comes of age, as God set the time in verse 4.

decisions.choice: managers
decisions.reason: "Steward" is now an uncommon word; "managers" says what these people did.

decisions.choice: a child who will inherit everything his father owns
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an heir is and repeats the estate so the picture is clear to a young reader.

decisions.choice: tutores y administradores
decisions.reason: "Tutor" is the Spanish legal word for the guardian of a minor, which is what the first word means here (m3), and it keeps this word apart from "guía", used for the household guardian of 3:24-25. "Administradores" says what the second group did, as the English "managers" does.

decisions.choice: wasimamizi na mawakili
decisions.reason: The first word is a guardian appointed over a minor (m3). "Mlezi" would be the most natural word, but it is kept for the household guardian of 3:24-25, a different Greek word, so "msimamizi" (one put in charge) is used here. "Wakili" is a steward who manages property. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: slave / a slave's
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it in Galatians 4–5: the slave who owns nothing is set against the heir who owns everything, and against the son and the freedom of 4:5-7.

decisions.choice: esclave at every level in 4:1-9, and through 4:21-5:1
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English have it: the slave who owns nothing is set against the heir, the son and the freedom of 4:5-7, so every level keeps "esclave".

decisions.choice: tuteurs et intendants
decisions.reason: "Tuteur" is the French legal word for the guardian of a minor, and "intendant" for the one who manages a household or estate (m3). "Gardien" is kept for the household slave of 3:24-25.

decisions.choice: mineur (B); un enfant (L); tant qu'il est jeune (R)
decisions.reason: The point is legal standing, not age in years (m1); French "mineur" says exactly that.

decisions.choice: "노예" at every level through 4:1-9 and 4:21-5:1
decisions.reason: Here slavery set against sonship and freedom is the point of Paul's picture (the English keeps "slave" at every level), so the style guide's "노예" is used, as in 3:28. "종" stays for Paul as Christ's servant (1:10).

decisions.choice: "후견인들과 관리인들"
decisions.reason: Those who had charge of a minor and of his property (the meaning decision). "후견인" (legal guardian) and "관리인" (manager) are the current words; "청지기" is older church language.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" at every level in 4:1-9
decisions.reason: Paul sets the slave against the son and heir, and slavery under the law and the powers against freedom (m2), so "nô lệ" stays at every level, under the rule for this word, as in 3:28.

decisions.choice: "người ấy" (L, B), "nó" (R) for the heir, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The heir is a boy in the picture Paul draws from family law (m1); Vietnamese "người ấy" and "nó" do not mark sex, and the English has no span either.

decisions.choice: menor (L); criança (B); pequeno (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "menor", the legal word for a minor, which is the point of m1 (legal standing, not age); Balanced and Readable use the everyday words.

decisions.choice: tutores e administradores
decisions.reason: "Tutor" is the Portuguese legal word for a guardian appointed for a minor, and "administrador" for someone who manages property (m3); "mordomo", the older word, now means a butler.

decisions.choice: አሳዳጊዎች (guardians) and መጋቢዎች (managers, stewards)
decisions.reason: These are the people who had charge of a minor and of his property (meaning decision m3). "ሞግዚት" is kept for the different word of 3:24-25, so here "አሳዳጊ", one who brings up and looks after a child, is paired with "መጋቢ", the steward who manages a household's goods.

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ἡμεῖς, ὅτε ἦμεν νήπιοι, ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου ἤμεθα δεδουλωμένοι·

records.literal_gloss: So also we, when we were children, under the elements of the world we were enslaved;

en.L: So also we, when we were children, were enslaved under the elements of the world.
en.B: In the same way we too, when we were children, were held as slaves under the elemental forces of the world.
en.R: It was the same for us. When we were like young children, we were slaves to the powers and rules that run this world.

es.L: Así también nosotros, cuando éramos niños, estábamos esclavizados bajo los elementos del mundo.
es.B: Del mismo modo, también nosotros, cuando éramos niños, vivíamos como esclavos bajo las fuerzas elementales del mundo.
es.R: Lo mismo nos pasaba a nosotros. Cuando éramos como niños pequeños, éramos esclavos de los poderes y las reglas que dominan este mundo.

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo sisi pia, tulipokuwa watoto, tulikuwa tumefanywa watumwa chini ya mambo ya msingi ya ulimwengu.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo nasi, tulipokuwa watoto, tulishikwa utumwani chini ya nguvu za msingi za ulimwengu.
sw.R: Ndivyo ilivyokuwa kwetu pia. Tulipokuwa kama watoto wadogo, tulikuwa watumwa wa nguvu na kanuni zinazotawala ulimwengu huu.

fr.L: De même nous aussi, quand nous étions enfants, nous étions réduits en esclavage sous les éléments du monde.
fr.B: De la même façon, nous aussi, quand nous étions des enfants, nous étions tenus en esclavage sous les forces élémentaires du monde.
fr.R: C’était pareil pour nous. Quand nous étions comme de jeunes enfants, nous étions esclaves des puissances et des règles qui dirigent ce monde.

ko.L: 이와 같이 우리도 어린아이였을 때에는 세상의 기초 원소들 아래서 노예로 지냈습니다.
ko.B: 이처럼 우리도 어린아이였을 때에는 세상의 근본 세력들 아래 노예로 매여 있었습니다.
ko.R: 우리도 마찬가지였습니다. 우리가 어린아이와 같았을 때, 우리는 이 세상을 다스리는 세력과 규칙의 노예였습니다.

vi.L: Chúng ta cũng vậy, khi chúng ta còn là trẻ nhỏ, chúng ta đã bị bắt làm nô lệ dưới các nguyên tố của thế gian.
vi.B: Cũng vậy, khi còn là trẻ nhỏ, chúng ta đã bị giam giữ làm nô lệ dưới các nguyên lực của thế gian.
vi.R: Chúng ta cũng giống như vậy. Khi chúng ta còn như những đứa trẻ, chúng ta làm nô lệ cho những quyền lực và luật lệ đang chi phối thế gian này.

pt.L: Assim também nós, quando éramos menores, estávamos escravizados debaixo dos elementos do mundo.
pt.B: Da mesma forma, nós também, quando éramos crianças, éramos mantidos como escravos debaixo das forças elementares do mundo.
pt.R: Foi a mesma coisa conosco. Quando éramos como crianças pequenas, éramos escravos dos poderes e das regras que governam este mundo.

am.L: እንዲሁም እኛ ደግሞ ሕፃናት በነበርን ጊዜ ከዓለም መሠረታዊ ነገሮች በታች ባሪያዎች ሆነን ነበር።
am.B: እንዲሁም እኛ ሕፃናት በነበርን ጊዜ ከዓለም መሠረታዊ ኃይላት በታች ባሪያዎች ሆነን ተይዘን ነበር።
am.R: እኛም እንደዚሁ ነበርን። እንደ ትንንሽ ልጆች በነበርን ጊዜ ይህን ዓለም ለሚገዙት ኃይላትና ሥርዓቶች ባሪያዎች ነበርን።

decisions.choice: we: Paul and all believers, Jews and Gentiles alike, before Christ came
alternatives: we Jews, who lived under the law
decisions.reason: The "we" could be Paul and his fellow Jews, held under the law as a guardian (3:23-25). But in verses 8-9 Paul tells the Galatians, who were Gentiles, that taking up the law would be turning back to the same elemental things they served before. So the "we" most likely includes everyone, each under the form of slavery that belonged to life before Christ.

decisions.choice: the elemental forces of the world: the basic powers and principles thought to govern life in this world, and the religious rules bound up with them
alternatives: the elementary principles or ABCs of religion
elemental spirits: spiritual beings ruling the world
decisions.reason: στοιχεῖα means the basic parts of something: the letters of the alphabet, the elements (earth, water, air, fire) of which the world was thought to be made, or the ABCs of a subject (Hebrews 5:12). In the thinking of the time the elements were linked with the stars and with spiritual powers. Here Paul ties them to slavery, to beings that are not gods (verse 8), and to keeping days and months and seasons (verse 10). So the phrase may mean the elementary rules of religion, Jewish and pagan alike, or the powers thought to rule the world through them; for Paul's readers the two belonged together. Colossians 2:8 and 2:20 use the same phrase.

decisions.choice: we were held as slaves: a lasting condition, not a single event
decisions.reason: The verb is a past tense with a perfect participle: a settled state of slavery, which the coming of the Son ends (verses 4-5).

decisions.choice: the elements of the world (L); the elemental forces of the world (B); the powers and rules that run this world (R)
alternatives: the basic principles of the world
the elemental spirits of the world
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 2:8: Literal keeps the bare word, Balanced uses a phrase that keeps both senses of m2 open, and Readable names both.

decisions.choice: like young children
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Paul is comparing believers to the heir under age in verse 1, not speaking of childhood.

decisions.choice: los elementos del mundo (L); las fuerzas elementales del mundo (B); los poderes y las reglas que dominan este mundo (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Colossians 2:8 and 2:20, so the reader can see Paul uses one phrase. "Rudimentos" would narrow the sense to the ABCs of religion; the chosen words keep both senses of m2 open. Verse 9 uses them again.

decisions.choice: mambo ya msingi ya ulimwengu (L); nguvu za msingi za ulimwengu (B); nguvu na kanuni zinazotawala ulimwengu huu (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as Colossians 2:8 and 2:20. "Mafundisho" (teachings) would narrow the sense to the ABCs alone; these keep both senses of m2 open. Verse 9 uses them again.

decisions.choice: held as slaves / slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery under the law or the elemental forces is set against freedom (Galatians 4–5). The slavery ends when the Son comes (m3).

decisions.choice: les éléments du monde (L); les forces élémentaires du monde (B); les puissances et les règles qui dirigent ce monde (R); the same in 4:9
decisions.reason: The French wording of Colossians 2:8 and 2:20 for the same phrase, so that the reader can see that Paul uses it in both letters (m2).

decisions.choice: "세상의 기초 원소들" (L); "세상의 근본 세력들" (B); "이 세상을 다스리는 세력과 규칙" (R), here and in verse 9
decisions.reason: The same words as in Colossians 2:8 and 2:20 for the same Greek phrase: Literal keeps the basic sense, Balanced keeps the powers in view, and Readable names both, as the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "các nguyên tố của thế gian" (L); "các nguyên lực của thế gian" (B); "những quyền lực và luật lệ đang chi phối thế gian này" (R); the same in 4:9
alternatives: "những nguyên lý sơ học của thế gian"
decisions.reason: The words of the Vietnamese Colossians (2:8) for the same Greek phrase. Balanced needs a word that keeps both senses of m2, basic forces and basic rules, and "nguyên lực" (elemental forces) does so without settling the question; Readable names both, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "chúng ta" for "we"
decisions.reason: Here "we" takes in all believers, Jews and Gentiles alike (m1), so the inclusive form.

decisions.choice: os elementos do mundo (L); as forças elementares do mundo (B); os poderes e as regras que governam este mundo (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal keeps the bare word, Balanced a phrase that leaves both senses of m2 open, and Readable names both. "Os rudimentos do mundo" would keep only the sense of basic lessons.

decisions.choice: የዓለም መሠረታዊ ነገሮች (L); የዓለም መሠረታዊ ኃይላት (B); ይህን ዓለም የሚገዙት ኃይላትና ሥርዓቶች (R), here and in 4:9
decisions.reason: The word names the basic powers and principles thought to rule life in this world, with the rules bound up with them (meaning decision m2). "ንጥረ ነገሮች" is now the chemist's word for elements, so Literal says "basic things" and Balanced and Readable name the powers, as the English does.

source.text: ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ, γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός, γενόμενον ὑπὸ νόμον, ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ, ἵνα τὴν υἱοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: But when came the fullness of the time, sent out the God the Son of him, having come to be from a woman, having come to be under law, \v 5 so that those under law he might redeem, so that the adoption we might receive.

en.L: But when the fullness of the time came, God sent out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, born of a woman, born under [the] law, \v 5 so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might redeem those under [the] law, so that we might receive the adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.B: But when the time God had set was complete, God sent out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. He was born of a woman and born under the law, \v 5 to redeem those who lived under the law, so that we might be adopted as {{gender:children|sons}}.
en.R: But when the right time came, God sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son. He was born of a woman, and born under the law. \v 5 God sent {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to buy freedom for those who were under the law, so that God could adopt us as {{gender:children|sons}}.

es.L: Pero cuando llegó la plenitud del tiempo, envió Dios a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, nacido de mujer, nacido bajo [la] ley, \v 5 para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} redimiera a los [que estaban] bajo [la] ley, a fin de que recibiéramos la adopción como hijos.
es.B: Pero cuando se cumplió el tiempo que Dios había fijado, Dios envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. Nació de una mujer y nació bajo la ley, \v 5 para redimir a quienes vivían bajo la ley, de modo que fuéramos adoptados como hijos.
es.R: Pero cuando llegó el momento justo, Dios envió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. Nació de una mujer, y nació bajo la ley. \v 5 Dios {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envió para comprar la libertad de los que estaban bajo la ley, para que Dios nos adoptara como hijos.

sw.L: Lakini utimilifu wa wakati ulipofika, Mungu alimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, aliyezaliwa kutoka kwa mwanamke, aliyezaliwa chini ya sheria, \v 5 ili awakomboe walio chini ya sheria, ili tupokee kufanywa wana.
sw.B: Lakini wakati ambao Mungu aliuweka ulipotimia, Mungu alimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Alizaliwa na mwanamke, akazaliwa chini ya sheria, \v 5 ili awakomboe watu walioishi chini ya sheria, nasi tufanywe wana.
sw.R: Lakini wakati unaofaa ulipofika, Mungu alimtuma Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Alizaliwa na mwanamke, na alizaliwa chini ya sheria. \v 5 Mungu alimtuma ili awanunulie uhuru wale waliokuwa chini ya sheria, ili Mungu atufanye kuwa watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

fr.L: Mais quand est venue la plénitude du temps, Dieu a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, né d’une femme, né sous la Loi, \v 5 afin qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rachète ceux [qui étaient] sous la Loi, afin que nous recevions l’adoption comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}.
fr.B: Mais quand le temps fixé par Dieu a été accompli, Dieu a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. Il est né d’une femme, né sous la Loi, \v 5 pour racheter ceux qui vivaient sous la Loi, afin que nous soyons adoptés comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}.
fr.R: Mais quand le bon moment est arrivé, Dieu a envoyé {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. Il est né d’une femme, et né sous la Loi. \v 5 Dieu {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a envoyé pour racheter la liberté de ceux qui étaient sous la Loi, pour que Dieu puisse nous adopter comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}.

ko.L: 그러나 때가 차매 하나님께서 그분의 아들을 보내셨습니다. [그 아들은] 여자에게서 나셨고 율법 아래 나셨으니, \v 5 율법 아래 있는 사람들을 속량하시고 우리가 {{gender:자녀|아들}}의 자격을 받게 하시려는 것이었습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 하나님께서 정하신 때가 차자, 하나님께서 그분의 아들을 보내셨습니다. 그 아들은 여자에게서 나셨고, 율법 아래 나셨습니다. \v 5 그것은 율법 아래 살던 사람들을 속량하셔서, 우리가 하나님의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}로 입양되게 하시려는 것이었습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 알맞은 때가 되자, 하나님께서 그분의 아들을 보내셨습니다. 그 아들은 여자에게서 태어나셨고, 율법 아래 태어나셨습니다. \v 5 하나님께서 그 아들을 보내신 것은 율법 아래 있던 사람들을 값을 치르고 자유롭게 하시려는 것이었습니다. 그래서 하나님께서 우리를 그분의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}로 입양하실 수 있게 하셨습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng khi thời điểm đã trọn, Đức Chúa Trời đã sai Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra, sinh bởi một người nữ, sinh ra dưới luật pháp, \v 5 để cứu chuộc những người ở dưới luật pháp, hầu cho chúng ta nhận được sự nhận làm con.
vi.B: Nhưng khi thời điểm Đức Chúa Trời đã định đến lúc trọn vẹn, Đức Chúa Trời đã sai Con của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến. Con ấy được sinh ra bởi một người nữ và sinh ra dưới luật pháp, \v 5 để cứu chuộc những người sống dưới luật pháp, hầu cho chúng ta được nhận làm con.
vi.R: Nhưng khi đến đúng thời điểm, Đức Chúa Trời đã sai Con của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến. Con ấy được một người phụ nữ sinh ra, và sinh ra dưới luật pháp. \v 5 Đức Chúa Trời sai Con đến để trả giá chuộc tự do cho những người ở dưới luật pháp, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhận chúng ta làm con.

pt.L: Mas, quando veio a plenitude do tempo, Deus enviou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho, nascido de mulher, nascido debaixo da Lei, \v 5 para que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} resgatasse os que estavam debaixo da Lei, a fim de recebermos a adoção como filhos.
pt.B: Mas, quando se completou o tempo que Deus tinha marcado, Deus enviou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho. Ele nasceu de mulher e nasceu debaixo da Lei, \v 5 para resgatar os que viviam debaixo da Lei, a fim de que fôssemos adotados como filhos.
pt.R: Mas, quando chegou o tempo certo, Deus enviou o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho. Ele nasceu de uma mulher e nasceu debaixo da Lei. \v 5 Deus {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} enviou para comprar a liberdade dos que estavam debaixo da Lei, para que Deus pudesse nos adotar como filhos.

am.L: የዘመኑ ሙላት በደረሰ ጊዜ ግን እግዚአብሔር ልጁን ላከ፤ [እርሱም] ከሴት የተወለደ፣ ከሕግ በታች የተወለደ ነው፤ \v 5 ይኸውም ከሕግ በታች ያሉትን ይዋጅ ዘንድ፣ እኛም ልጅነትን እንቀበል ዘንድ ነው።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር የወሰነው ጊዜ በተፈጸመ ጊዜ ግን ልጁን ላከ። እርሱም ከሴት ተወለደ፤ ከሕግም በታች ተወለደ። \v 5 ይህም ከሕግ በታች የነበሩትን ሊዋጅና እኛም በልጅነት እንድንወሰድ ነው።
am.R: ትክክለኛው ጊዜ በደረሰ ጊዜ ግን እግዚአብሔር ልጁን ላከ። እርሱም ከሴት ተወለደ፤ ከሕግም በታች ተወለደ። \v 5 እግዚአብሔር የላከው ከሕግ በታች የነበሩትን ዋጋ ከፍሎ ነፃ እንዲያወጣቸው ነው፤ ይህም እግዚአብሔር እኛን ልጆቹ አድርጎ እንዲወስደን ነው።

decisions.choice: the fullness of the time: the moment God had set
alternatives: simply "when the time was right" in a general sense
decisions.reason: The phrase answers "the time set beforehand by the father" in verse 2. The time of slavery ran until the date God had fixed, and then it was complete.

decisions.choice: God sent out his Son from himself
alternatives: God commissioned a man for a task, as he sent the prophets
decisions.reason: ἐξαποστέλλω means to send someone out on a mission. Paul uses the same verb for the Spirit in verse 6. He speaks of the one sent as already God's Son when he was sent, and only then of his birth, which fits his teaching elsewhere that the Son was with God before he came (Philippians 2:6-7).

decisions.choice: born of a woman, born under the law: truly human, and a Jew under Moses' law
alternatives: a statement about the virgin birth
decisions.reason: γίνομαι means "to come to be" and is used of birth. "Born of a woman" was a common way of saying "a human being" (Job 14:1; Matthew 11:11). Paul is not discussing how Jesus was conceived; he is saying the Son shared the condition of those he came to free. "Under the law" means he lived as a Jew under Moses' law, the very place of those he redeems.

decisions.choice: redeem: buy out of slavery, set free at a price
alternatives: rescue, without the idea of a price
decisions.reason: ἐξαγοράζω is the verb of 3:13, where Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. It comes from the marketplace: buying someone out of another's ownership.

decisions.choice: adoption as sons: being made a son and heir by law
alternatives: adoption as children, without the idea of heirship
decisions.reason: υἱοθεσία is the legal word for adoption. In Roman law an adopted son received the full rights of a son born into the family, including the inheritance. In this family the inheritance and the standing went with sonship, and Paul gives that standing to every believer, women as much as men (3:28-29).

decisions.choice: adoption as {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The word gives the standing of a son and heir (m5), which Paul gives to men and women alike. The inclusive default says who is adopted; the traditional setting keeps "sons", which shows the legal standing more plainly.

decisions.choice: the time God had set was complete (B); the right time came (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sense of a time filled up to its set point; Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: God sent him to buy freedom for
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence, so it repeats who sent the Son, and it explains "redeem" as buying someone's freedom (m4).

decisions.choice: hijos, no gender setting
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "children" with "sons" as the traditional form, Spanish "hijos" already covers sons and daughters and keeps the heir's standing that adoption carries (m5), as in Ephesians 1:5. So verses 5-7 have no gender span.

decisions.choice: wana, no gender setting
decisions.reason: "Kufanywa wana" is adoption with an heir's standing (m5), and "wana" already includes sons and daughters, as in Ephesians 1:5. A male-only alternative would change the meaning, so verses 5-7 have no gender span.

decisions.choice: adoptés comme {{gender:enfants|fils}}; {{gender:enfants|fils}} and {{gender:enfant|fils}} in 4:6-7
decisions.reason: As in 3:26: the legal standing of a son and heir is given to women and men alike (m5), so "enfants" is the default and "fils" the traditional alternative that shows the legal standing. "Le Fils" of God in verses 4 and 6 takes no setting.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:자녀|아들}}의 자격" (L); "{{gender:자녀|아들}}로 입양되다" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means being made a son and heir by law (the meaning decision). "양자" (adopted son) is the traditional word but names a son only; Korean "입양" (adoption) with the setting lets the reader choose "자녀" or "아들", as the English does. Literal says "자격" (standing), close to the Greek's one noun.

decisions.choice: "때가 차매" (L); "하나님께서 정하신 때가 차자" (B); "알맞은 때가 되자" (R)
decisions.reason: The fullness of time is the moment God had set (the meaning decision). Literal keeps the short phrase "때가 차매", a set expression still understood in Korean; Balanced says who set it, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "sự nhận làm con" (L), "được nhận làm con" (B), "nhận chúng ta làm con" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Adoption is being made a son and heir by law (m5). Vietnamese "con" takes in sons and daughters, so the English span has nothing to choose between, as in the Vietnamese Romans (8:15).

decisions.choice: "Con ấy" (B), "Con" (R) as subject
decisions.reason: "Ngài" in this sentence stands for both God and the Son, so Balanced and Readable name the Son, as the Vietnamese Colossians does (1:14).

decisions.choice: adoção como filhos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "children|sons" under the gender setting. Portuguese "filhos" includes sons and daughters and keeps the standing of a son and heir (m5), as in 3:7, 3:26 and Romans 8:15, so no setting is needed; the same in verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: capitalised pronouns, as the English alternative has them
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns for God and for Christ are written plainly through the letter.

decisions.choice: ልጅነት (adoption, sonship), with no gender span; ልጅ, ልጆች in 4:6-7 also without a span
alternatives: a span such as the English {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: "ልጅነት" is being made a child and heir by law (meaning decision m5), and "ልጅ" and "ልጆች" cover daughters as well as sons, so Amharic has no second wording for the setting to offer, as in Romans 8.

source.text: ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοί, ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν, κρᾶζον· Αββα ὁ πατήρ.

records.literal_gloss: And because you are sons, sent out the God the Spirit of the Son of him into the hearts of us, crying, Abba, the Father.

en.L: And because you are {{gender:children|sons}}, God sent out the Spirit of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son into our hearts, crying, "Abba, Father!"
en.B: And since you are {{gender:children|sons}}, God has sent out the Spirit of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son into our hearts, and the Spirit cries, "Abba, Father!"
en.R: You are God's {{gender:children|sons}}, and because of that, God has put the Spirit of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son in our hearts. The Spirit cries out to God, "Abba! Father!"

es.L: Y porque {{plural_you:son|sois}} hijos, envió Dios el Espíritu de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo a nuestros corazones, clamando: «¡Abba, Padre!»
es.B: Y como {{plural_you:son|sois}} hijos, Dios ha enviado a nuestros corazones el Espíritu de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, y el Espíritu clama: «¡Abba, Padre!»
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} hijos de Dios, y por eso Dios ha puesto en nuestros corazones el Espíritu de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo. El Espíritu clama a Dios: «¡Abba! ¡Padre!»

sw.L: Na kwa kuwa ninyi ni wana, Mungu alimtuma Roho wa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ndani ya mioyo yetu, akiita, "Aba, Baba!"
sw.B: Na kwa kuwa ninyi ni wana, Mungu amemtuma Roho wa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} aingie mioyoni mwetu, naye Roho anaita, "Aba, Baba!"
sw.R: Ninyi ni wana wa Mungu, na kwa sababu hiyo Mungu amemweka Roho wa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ndani ya mioyo yetu. Roho huyo anamlilia Mungu, "Aba! Baba!"

fr.L: Et parce que vous êtes {{gender:enfants|fils}}, Dieu a envoyé dans nos cœurs l’Esprit de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, qui crie : « Abba, Père ! »
fr.B: Et parce que vous êtes {{gender:enfants|fils}}, Dieu a envoyé dans nos cœurs l’Esprit de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, et l’Esprit crie : « Abba, Père ! »
fr.R: Vous êtes les {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Dieu, et c’est pour cela que Dieu a mis dans nos cœurs l’Esprit de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils. L’Esprit crie vers Dieu : « Abba ! Père ! »

ko.L: 그리고 여러분이 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이므로, 하나님께서 그분의 아들의 영을 우리 마음속에 보내셔서 "아바, 아버지!" 하고 부르짖게 하셨습니다.
ko.B: 여러분이 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이기 때문에, 하나님께서는 그분의 아들의 영을 우리 마음속에 보내 주셨습니다. 그 영께서 "아바, 아버지!" 하고 부르짖으십니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 하나님의 {{gender:자녀|아들}}들입니다. 그래서 하나님께서는 그분의 아들의 영을 우리 마음속에 넣어 주셨습니다. 성령께서 하나님께 "아바! 아버지!" 하고 부르짖으십니다.

vi.L: Và vì anh chị em là con, nên Đức Chúa Trời đã sai Thánh Linh của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào lòng chúng ta, kêu lên: "A-ba, Cha!"
vi.B: Và vì anh chị em là con, nên Đức Chúa Trời đã sai Thánh Linh của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào lòng chúng ta, và Thánh Linh kêu lên: "A-ba, Cha!"
vi.R: Anh chị em là con cái của Đức Chúa Trời, và vì vậy, Đức Chúa Trời đã đặt Thánh Linh của Con {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào lòng chúng ta. Thánh Linh kêu lên với Đức Chúa Trời: "A-ba! Cha!"

pt.L: E, porque vocês são filhos, Deus enviou o Espírito do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho aos nossos corações, clamando: "Aba, Pai!"
pt.B: E, porque vocês são filhos, Deus enviou ao nosso coração o Espírito do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho, e o Espírito clama: "Aba, Pai!"
pt.R: Vocês são filhos de Deus, e por isso Deus colocou no nosso coração o Espírito do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} Filho. O Espírito clama a Deus: "Aba! Pai!"

am.L: ልጆች ስለ ሆናችሁም፣ እግዚአብሔር የልጁን መንፈስ ወደ ልባችን ላከ፤ [እርሱም] «አባ፣ አባት!» እያለ ይጮኻል።
am.B: ልጆች ስለ ሆናችሁ እግዚአብሔር የልጁን መንፈስ ወደ ልባችን ልኳል፤ መንፈሱም «አባ፣ አባት!» እያለ ይጮኻል።

decisions.choice: because you are sons, God sent the Spirit
alternatives: to show that you are sons, God sent the Spirit
decisions.reason: ὅτι here most naturally gives the reason: God gives the Spirit to those who are already his sons. Some read it as "the proof that you are sons is that God sent the Spirit", which fits 3:2-5, where receiving the Spirit is the sign that they belong. Either way, having the Spirit and being God's sons go together.

decisions.choice: sons: the standing of a son and heir, given to all believers
decisions.reason: υἱός is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir: in this setting daughters did not usually inherit as sons did. Paul gives that full standing to every believer, and he has just said that in Christ there is neither male nor female (3:28-29), so women share it on the same terms as men.

decisions.choice: into our hearts: Paul moves from "you" to "us"
decisions.reason: Paul begins with "you are sons" and ends with "our hearts": he and the Galatians receive the same Spirit, Jew and Gentile alike.

decisions.choice: Abba: the Aramaic word for "father", followed by the Greek word
decisions.reason: Αββα is the Aramaic word a child used for a father, and the word Jesus used in his own prayer (Mark 14:36). The Greek churches kept the Aramaic word and added its translation, as Romans 8:15 also does. Believers address God the way the Son does.

decisions.choice: the Spirit cries out
alternatives: we cry out, moved by the Spirit
decisions.reason: The participle κρᾶζον agrees with the word for Spirit, so it is the Spirit who cries out in believers' hearts. In Romans 8:15 it is "we" who cry "Abba"; the two passages describe the same prayer from two sides.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: As in verse 5: the inclusive default names everyone who has this standing, and the traditional setting keeps "sons".

decisions.choice: and the Spirit cries (B); the Spirit cries out to God (R)
decisions.reason: English needs the subject of the participle made clear (m5), and the Spirit is never "it".

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: As throughout Paul's letters, each plural "you" addressed to the Galatians and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (the default) or vosotros.

decisions.choice: Aba
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is kept, followed by "Baba" as the Greek gives its translation (m4). Swahili spelling does not write doubled consonants, so the word is written "Aba".

decisions.choice: « Abba, Père ! », with Abba kept at every level
decisions.reason: Paul keeps the Aramaic word and adds its Greek translation (m4), and French does the same. "Papa" would make the child's word too casual for public reading and lose the word Jesus himself used.

decisions.choice: "아바, 아버지" at every level
decisions.reason: Paul gives the Aramaic word for "father" and then the Greek one (the meaning decision). Korean writes the Aramaic word as "아바", the form Korean readers know from the Bible; "아빠" (daddy) looks the same but is a Korean word, and would make the Aramaic sound like Korean baby talk. A reviewer may prefer "아빠", which some readers find closer in feeling.

decisions.choice: the honorific for the Spirit: "그 영께서 ... 부르짖으십니다" (B); "성령께서" (R)
decisions.reason: The Spirit of God's Son is God's own Spirit, so Korean gives him the honorific -시- and 께서, as it does for God and Christ.

decisions.choice: "A-ba, Cha!"
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is kept in the form of the Vietnamese Mark (14:36) and Romans (8:15), followed by "Cha", as the Greek gives the word and its meaning (m4).

decisions.choice: Aba
decisions.reason: As in Romans 8:15: the Aramaic word is spelled as Portuguese writes its sounds (style section 11), followed by its translation "Pai", as the Greek does (m4).

decisions.choice: «አባ፣ አባት!»
decisions.reason: Paul gives the Aramaic word for father and then the Greek one (meaning decision m4). "አባ" is also an Amharic word for father, so the Amharic reader hears both words as Paul's first readers did; the same wording is used in Romans 8:15.

source.text: ὥστε οὐκέτι εἶ δοῦλος ἀλλὰ υἱός· εἰ δὲ υἱός, καὶ κληρονόμος διὰ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So no longer are you a slave but a son; and if a son, also an heir through God.

en.L: So you are no longer a slave but {{gender:a child|a son}}, and if {{gender:a child|a son}}, also an heir through God.
en.B: So you are no longer a slave but {{gender:a child|a son}}, and if you are {{gender:a child|a son}}, then you are also an heir, made so by God.
en.R: So you are not a slave anymore. You are God's {{gender:child|son}}. And since you are God's {{gender:child|son}}, God has made you an heir as well.

es.L: De modo que ya no eres esclavo, sino hijo; y si [eres] hijo, [eres] también heredero por medio de Dios.
es.B: Así pues, ya no eres esclavo, sino hijo; y si eres hijo, eres también heredero, y lo eres por obra de Dios.
es.R: Así que ya no eres esclavo. Eres hijo de Dios. Y como eres hijo de Dios, Dios te ha hecho también heredero.

sw.L: Hivyo wewe si mtumwa tena, bali ni mwana; na ikiwa ni mwana, ni mrithi pia kupitia Mungu.
sw.B: Basi wewe si mtumwa tena, bali ni mwana; na ikiwa wewe ni mwana, basi wewe ni mrithi pia, na Mungu ndiye aliyekufanya hivyo.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wewe si mtumwa tena. Wewe ni mtoto wa Mungu. Na kwa kuwa wewe ni mtoto wa Mungu, Mungu amekufanya pia kuwa mrithi.

fr.L: Ainsi tu n’es plus esclave, mais {{gender:enfant|fils}} ; et si [tu es] {{gender:enfant|fils}}, [tu es] aussi héritier par Dieu.
fr.B: Ainsi, tu n’es plus esclave, mais {{gender:enfant|fils}} ; et si tu es {{gender:enfant|fils}}, tu es aussi héritier, et c’est Dieu qui t’a fait tel.
fr.R: Ainsi, tu n’es plus un esclave. Tu es {{gender:enfant|fils}} de Dieu. Et puisque tu es {{gender:enfant|fils}} de Dieu, Dieu a fait aussi de toi un héritier.

ko.L: 그러므로 당신은 더 이상 노예가 아니라 {{gender:자녀|아들}}입니다. 그리고 {{gender:자녀|아들}}이면 하나님을 통하여 상속자이기도 합니다.
ko.B: 그러므로 당신은 더 이상 노예가 아니라 {{gender:자녀|아들}}입니다. 그리고 {{gender:자녀|아들}}이라면 하나님께서 당신을 상속자로 세우셨습니다.

pt.L: Assim, você já não é escravo, mas filho; e, se [é] filho, também [é] herdeiro por meio de Deus.
pt.B: Assim, você já não é escravo, mas filho; e, se é filho, também é herdeiro, por obra de Deus.
pt.R: Por isso, você não é mais escravo. Você é filho de Deus. E, como é filho de Deus, Deus também fez de você um herdeiro.

am.L: ስለዚህ ከእንግዲህ ወዲህ ባሪያ አይደለህም፤ ልጅ ነህ እንጂ፤ ልጅ ከሆንክም በእግዚአብሔር በኩል ደግሞ ወራሽ ነህ።
am.B: ስለዚህ ከእንግዲህ ባሪያ አይደለህም፤ ልጅ ነህ፤ ልጅ ከሆንክ ደግሞ እግዚአብሔር ወራሽ አድርጎሃል።

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "an heir through God"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Many later ones read "an heir of God through Christ", and a few have other wordings. The SBLGNT follows early manuscripts with the short reading "through God", which copyists seem to have filled out because it is unusual. The meaning is the same: the inheritance is God's gift.

decisions.choice: you, singular: each believer in person
decisions.reason: Paul has spoken to the Galatians as a group; here he turns to each one individually. What is true of the church is true of every member.

decisions.choice: son: the standing of a son and heir, given to all believers
decisions.reason: υἱός is the word for a son, and in a family it carried the standing of a son and heir: in this setting daughters did not usually inherit as sons did. Paul gives that full standing to every believer, and he has just said that in Christ there is neither male nor female (3:28-29), so women share it on the same terms as men.

decisions.choice: heir: one who will receive what God promised Abraham
decisions.reason: κληρονόμος takes up the picture of verse 1 and the promise of 3:18 and 3:29. The inheritance is what God promised Abraham and his offspring, received now through the Spirit (3:14) and in full later.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a child|a son}}
decisions.reason: As in verses 5-6.

decisions.choice: made so by God (B); God has made you an heir (R)
decisions.reason: "Through God" means God is the one who makes them heirs; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: eres (tú), no setting
decisions.reason: Paul turns from the church to each believer, with a singular "you" (m2). Spanish keeps the singular "tú", which needs no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: here the slave is set against the son and heir.

decisions.choice: tu, singular, in this verse
decisions.reason: Paul turns from the whole church to each believer (m2). French can show the singular, as English cannot, so every level says "tu" here.

decisions.choice: the singular "you" as "당신" at every level
decisions.reason: Paul turns to the singular "you", speaking to each believer in person (the meaning decision). Korean "당신", in the 합쇼체 of the letter, marks the change from "여러분" and is the form used for a general "you" in a written address, as in Romans 8:2.

decisions.choice: "bạn" for the singular "you"
decisions.reason: Paul turns to each believer in the singular (m2). As in the Vietnamese Romans (2:1; 8:2), the one reader addressed directly is "bạn"; "anh chị em" would make it plural.

decisions.choice: você (singular)
decisions.reason: Paul turns from the church to each believer (m2), and Portuguese can show it as English cannot: "você", the singular, at every level.

decisions.choice: አንተ (singular you): ባሪያ አይደለህም, ልጅ ነህ
decisions.reason: Paul turns from "you" plural to the singular, speaking to each believer in person (meaning decision m2); Amharic marks the singular on every verb, so it comes through without a note in the text.

source.text: Ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν οὐκ εἰδότες θεὸν ἐδουλεύσατε τοῖς φύσει μὴ οὖσι θεοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: But then indeed not knowing God you were slaves to the [ones] by nature not being gods;

en.L: But at that time, not knowing God, you were slaves to those [that] by nature are not gods.
en.B: In the past you did not know God, and you were slaves to beings that are not gods by nature.
en.R: Before, when you did not know God, you were slaves to gods that are not really gods at all.

es.L: Pero en aquel tiempo, no conociendo a Dios, {{plural_you:servían|servíais}} como esclavos a los que por naturaleza no son dioses.
es.B: En el pasado {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no {{plural_you:conocían|conocíais}} a Dios, y {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos de seres que por naturaleza no son dioses.
es.R: Antes, cuando no {{plural_you:conocían|conocíais}} a Dios, {{plural_you:eran|erais}} esclavos de dioses que en realidad no son dioses.

sw.L: Lakini wakati huo, mkiwa hamumjui Mungu, mlikuwa watumwa wa wale wasio miungu kwa asili yao.
sw.B: Zamani hamkumjua Mungu, nanyi mlikuwa watumwa wa viumbe ambavyo kwa asili si miungu.
sw.R: Hapo zamani hamkumjua Mungu, na mlikuwa watumwa wa miungu isiyo miungu kweli hata kidogo.

fr.L: Mais autrefois, ne connaissant pas Dieu, vous étiez esclaves de ceux qui par nature ne sont pas des dieux.
fr.B: Autrefois, vous ne connaissiez pas Dieu, et vous étiez esclaves d’êtres qui, par nature, ne sont pas des dieux.
fr.R: Avant, quand vous ne connaissiez pas Dieu, vous étiez esclaves de dieux qui n’en sont pas vraiment.

ko.L: 그러나 그때에는 여러분이 하나님을 알지 못하여, 본성상 신이 아닌 것들에게 노예로 지냈습니다.
ko.B: 전에 여러분은 하나님을 알지 못했고, 본래 신이 아닌 것들의 노예가 되어 있었습니다.
ko.R: 예전에 여러분이 하나님을 알지 못했을 때, 여러분은 사실은 신이 전혀 아닌 신들의 노예였습니다.

vi.L: Nhưng trước kia, khi chưa biết Đức Chúa Trời, anh chị em đã làm nô lệ cho những thần mà bản chất không phải là thần.
vi.B: Trước kia anh chị em không biết Đức Chúa Trời, và anh chị em đã làm nô lệ cho những thần mà bản chất không phải là thần.
vi.R: Trước đây, khi anh chị em chưa biết Đức Chúa Trời, anh chị em đã làm nô lệ cho những thần chẳng phải là thần thật chút nào.

pt.L: Mas naquele tempo, não conhecendo a Deus, vocês eram escravos dos que por natureza não são deuses.
pt.B: No passado vocês não conheciam a Deus e eram escravos de seres que por natureza não são deuses.
pt.R: Antes, quando vocês não conheciam a Deus, eram escravos de deuses que na verdade não são deuses.

am.L: ነገር ግን ያን ጊዜ እግዚአብሔርን ሳታውቁ፣ በባሕርያቸው አማልክት ላልሆኑት ባሪያዎች ነበራችሁ።
am.B: ቀድሞ እግዚአብሔርን አታውቁም ነበር፤ በባሕርያቸው አማልክት ላልሆኑ ፍጡራን ባሪያዎች ነበራችሁ።
am.R: ከዚህ በፊት እግዚአብሔርን ሳታውቁ በነበራችሁ ጊዜ፣ በእውነት አማልክት ላልሆኑ አማልክት ባሪያዎች ነበራችሁ።

decisions.choice: at that time: the Galatians' pagan past
decisions.reason: Paul now speaks to the Galatians as former Gentile worshipers. "At that time" is set against "now" in verse 9.

decisions.choice: beings that by nature are not gods
alternatives: idols that are nothing at all
spiritual powers that are real but not divine
decisions.reason: Paul does not say whether these "gods" are nothing or are real powers falsely worshiped. Elsewhere he says an idol is nothing (1 Corinthians 8:4) but also that pagan sacrifices are offered to demons (1 Corinthians 10:19-20). Here his point is only that whatever they are, they are not gods by nature.

decisions.choice: you were slaves to them
decisions.reason: δουλεύω means to serve as a slave. It keeps the picture of slavery from verses 1-7: their former religion was a kind of bondage.

decisions.choice: beings (B); gods that are not really gods at all (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek article stands for whatever is worshiped. Balanced names them as beings; Readable repeats "gods" to make the contrast plain. Neither decides whether they are real powers (m2).

decisions.choice: viumbe (beings)
decisions.reason: Balanced names what was worshiped, as the English does. "Vitu" would make them lifeless things and decide m2; "viumbe" leaves open whether they are idols or spiritual powers.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery under the law or the elemental forces is set against freedom (Galatians 4–5). The former religion of the Galatians was bondage (m3).

decisions.choice: "những thần mà bản chất không phải là thần"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision leaves open what these beings are (m2). "Thần" keeps the word "gods", lowercase, and "bản chất" says "by nature" without deciding whether they are spirits or nothing at all.

source.text: νῦν δὲ γνόντες θεόν, μᾶλλον δὲ γνωσθέντες ὑπὸ θεοῦ, πῶς ἐπιστρέφετε πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ ἀσθενῆ καὶ πτωχὰ στοιχεῖα, οἷς πάλιν ἄνωθεν δουλεύειν θέλετε;

records.literal_gloss: but now having known God, rather but having been known by God, how do you turn again to the weak and poor elements, to which again from above to be slaves you want?

en.L: But now, having come to know God, or rather having been known by God, how [is it that] you are turning back again to the weak and poor elements, to which you want to be enslaved all over again?
en.B: But now that you have come to know God, or rather to be known by God, how can you go back to those weak and worthless elemental forces and want to serve them as slaves once more?
en.R: But now you know God. Even more, God knows you as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own. So how can you turn back to those weak and useless powers and rules? Do you really want to be their slaves all over again?

es.L: pero ahora, habiendo conocido a Dios, o mejor dicho, habiendo sido conocidos por Dios, ¿cómo [es que] {{plural_you:se vuelven|os volvéis}} otra vez a los elementos débiles y pobres, a los cuales {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} servir como esclavos otra vez desde el principio?
es.B: Pero ahora que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} llegado a conocer a Dios, o mejor dicho, a ser conocidos por Dios, ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} volver a esas fuerzas elementales débiles y sin valor, y querer servirlas como esclavos una vez más?
es.R: Pero ahora {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} a Dios. Más aún, Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} conoce como {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}. Entonces, ¿cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} volver a esos poderes y reglas tan débiles e inútiles? ¿De verdad {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ser sus esclavos otra vez desde el principio?

sw.L: lakini sasa, mkiwa mmemjua Mungu, au tuseme, mkiwa mmejulikana na Mungu, mnarudije tena kwa mambo ya msingi dhaifu na maskini, ambayo mnapenda kuyatumikia kama watumwa tena, kuanzia mwanzo?
sw.B: Lakini sasa mmekuja kumjua Mungu, au zaidi ya hilo, mmekuja kujulikana na Mungu. Basi mnawezaje kurudi kwenye nguvu zile za msingi zilizo dhaifu na zisizo na thamani, mkitaka kuzitumikia kama watumwa tena?
sw.R: Lakini sasa mnamjua Mungu. Zaidi ya hayo, Mungu anawajua kuwa ni watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}. Basi mnawezaje kurudi kwenye nguvu na kanuni zile dhaifu zisizofaa kitu? Je, kweli mnataka kuwa watumwa wa mambo hayo tena, kama mwanzo?

fr.L: Mais maintenant, ayant connu Dieu, ou plutôt ayant été connus de Dieu, comment retournez-vous encore à ces éléments faibles et pauvres, que vous voulez de nouveau servir en esclaves, comme au commencement ?
fr.B: Mais maintenant que vous avez appris à connaître Dieu, ou plutôt que vous avez été connus de Dieu, comment pouvez-vous retourner à ces forces élémentaires faibles et sans valeur, et vouloir de nouveau les servir comme des esclaves ?
fr.R: Mais maintenant, vous connaissez Dieu. Bien plus, Dieu vous connaît, et vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez. Alors comment pouvez-vous retourner vers ces puissances et ces règles faibles et inutiles ? Voulez-vous vraiment redevenir leurs esclaves ?

ko.L: 그러나 이제는 여러분이 하나님을 알게 되었는데, 아니 오히려 하나님께 알려지게 되었는데, 어떻게 약하고 초라한 기초 원소들로 다시 돌아가서, 그것들에게 처음부터 다시 노예 노릇을 하려고 합니까?
ko.B: 그러나 이제 여러분은 하나님을 알게 되었습니다. 아니, 하나님께서 여러분을 알아주셨습니다. 그런데 어떻게 그 약하고 보잘것없는 근본 세력들로 되돌아가서, 다시 처음부터 그것들에게 노예 노릇을 하려고 합니까?
ko.R: 그러나 이제 여러분은 하나님을 압니다. 아니, 그보다 하나님께서 여러분을 그분의 사람으로 아십니다. 그런데 어떻게 그 약하고 쓸모없는 세력과 규칙으로 다시 돌아갈 수 있습니까? 정말 다시 처음부터 그것들의 노예가 되고 싶습니까?

vi.L: nhưng bây giờ, đã biết Đức Chúa Trời, đúng hơn là đã được Đức Chúa Trời biết, sao anh chị em lại quay trở về với các nguyên tố yếu ớt và nghèo nàn, mà anh chị em muốn làm nô lệ cho chúng một lần nữa từ đầu?
vi.B: Nhưng bây giờ anh chị em đã biết Đức Chúa Trời, hay đúng hơn là đã được Đức Chúa Trời biết đến, sao anh chị em còn quay trở lại với các nguyên lực yếu ớt và vô giá trị ấy, và lại muốn làm nô lệ cho chúng một lần nữa?
vi.R: Nhưng bây giờ anh chị em đã biết Đức Chúa Trời. Hơn thế nữa, Đức Chúa Trời biết anh chị em là người của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Vậy sao anh chị em lại có thể quay về với những quyền lực và luật lệ yếu ớt và vô dụng ấy? Anh chị em thật sự muốn làm nô lệ cho chúng một lần nữa sao?

pt.L: Mas agora, tendo conhecido a Deus, ou antes, tendo sido conhecidos por Deus, como [é que] vocês estão voltando outra vez aos elementos fracos e pobres, aos quais querem ser escravizados de novo, desde o começo?
pt.B: Mas agora que vocês conhecem a Deus, ou melhor, que são conhecidos por Deus, como podem voltar para essas forças elementares fracas e sem valor, e querer servi-las como escravos mais uma vez?
pt.R: Mas agora vocês conhecem a Deus. Mais do que isso: Deus conhece vocês como {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}}. Então, como vocês podem voltar para aqueles poderes e regras fracos e inúteis? Vocês querem mesmo ser escravos deles de novo?

am.L: አሁን ግን እግዚአብሔርን ካወቃችሁ፣ ይልቁንም በእግዚአብሔር ከታወቃችሁ በኋላ፣ እንደ ገና ደግሞ ከመጀመሪያው ባሪያዎች ልትሆኑላቸው ወደምትፈልጉት ወደ ደካሞቹና ወደ ድሆቹ መሠረታዊ ነገሮች እንዴት እንደ ገና ትመለሳላችሁ?
am.B: አሁን ግን እግዚአብሔርን አውቃችኋል፤ ይልቁንም በእግዚአብሔር ታውቃችኋል። ታዲያ ወደ እነዚያ ደካማና ከንቱ መሠረታዊ ኃይላት እንዴት ትመለሳላችሁ? እንደ ገናስ ባሪያዎች ሆናችሁ ልታገለግሏቸው እንዴት ትፈልጋላችሁ?
am.R: አሁን ግን እግዚአብሔርን ታውቃላችሁ። ከዚህም በላይ እግዚአብሔር የራሱ አድርጎ ያውቃችኋል። ታዲያ ወደ እነዚያ ደካማና የማይጠቅሙ ኃይላትና ሥርዓቶች እንዴት ትመለሳላችሁ? በእርግጥ እንደ ገና ባሪያዎቻቸው ልትሆኑ ትፈልጋላችሁን?

decisions.choice: known by God: God has taken them as his own
alternatives: God has become aware of them
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures, God's "knowing" people means choosing them and making them his own (Amos 3:2; 1 Corinthians 8:3). Paul corrects himself: their knowing God is real, but it rests on God's first knowing them.

decisions.choice: the weak and poor elemental forces: the same "elements" as verse 3
decisions.reason: στοιχεῖον is the word of verse 3; see the note there. They are "weak" because they cannot set anyone free, and "poor" because they have nothing to give, unlike the inheritance of verse 7.

decisions.choice: turning back again: taking up the law would be a return to slavery
decisions.reason: The Galatians are being urged to keep the Jewish law, not to return to idols. Yet Paul calls it turning back "again". Living under the law as the way to belong to God would put them back under the same kind of bondage they knew as pagans, because both belong to the time before Christ.

decisions.choice: all over again: from the beginning once more
decisions.reason: πάλιν ἄνωθεν doubles the idea of "again": they would be going back to the very start.

decisions.choice: elements (L); elemental forces (B); powers and rules (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: worthless (B); useless (R)
decisions.reason: "Poor" here means having nothing to give; Balanced and Readable use a word that says that.

decisions.choice: God knows you as his own
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what being known by God means (m1).

decisions.choice: serve them as slaves / be their slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery under the law or the elemental forces is set against freedom (Galatians 4–5). Turning back would be a return to slavery (m3).

decisions.choice: Dieu vous connaît, et vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartenez (R)
alternatives: Dieu vous connaît comme les siens
decisions.reason: Readable says what being known by God means (m1), as the English "as his own" does; French puts it as belonging, so that the pronoun for God can carry its setting.

decisions.choice: "được Đức Chúa Trời biết" (L), "được Đức Chúa Trời biết đến" (B); "Đức Chúa Trời biết anh chị em là người của Ngài" (R)
decisions.reason: To be known by God is to be taken as his own (m1). Literal keeps the turn from active to passive; Balanced adds "đến", which in Vietnamese carries the sense of being acknowledged, and Readable says it plainly, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἡμέρας παρατηρεῖσθε καὶ μῆνας καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἐνιαυτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Days you observe and months and seasons and years.

en.L: You are observing days and months and seasons and years.
en.B: You keep special days and months, seasons and years.
en.R: You carefully keep special days and months and seasons and years.

es.L: {{plural_you:Están|Estáis}} observando días y meses y estaciones y años.
es.B: {{plural_you:Guardan|Guardáis}} días especiales y meses, estaciones y años.
es.R: {{plural_you:Guardan|Guardáis}} con mucho cuidado días especiales, meses, estaciones y años.

sw.L: Mnazingatia siku na miezi na majira na miaka.
sw.B: Mnaadhimisha siku maalum, na miezi, majira na miaka.
sw.R: Mnaadhimisha kwa uangalifu mkubwa siku maalum, na miezi, majira na miaka.

fr.L: Vous observez des jours et des mois et des saisons et des années.
fr.B: Vous observez des jours sacrés, des mois, des saisons et des années.
fr.R: Vous respectez avec soin des jours spéciaux, et aussi des mois, des saisons et des années.

ko.L: 여러분은 날들과 달들과 절기들과 해들을 지키고 있습니다.
ko.B: 여러분은 특별한 날과 달과 절기와 해를 지키고 있습니다.
ko.R: 여러분은 특별한 날과 달과 절기와 해를 아주 꼼꼼하게 지키고 있습니다.

vi.L: Anh chị em đang giữ các ngày, các tháng, các mùa và các năm.
vi.B: Anh chị em giữ những ngày đặc biệt, những tháng, những mùa và những năm.
vi.R: Anh chị em cẩn thận giữ những ngày đặc biệt, những tháng, những mùa và những năm.

pt.L: Vocês observam dias, e meses, e estações, e anos.
pt.B: Vocês guardam dias especiais e meses, estações e anos.
pt.R: Vocês guardam com todo o cuidado dias especiais, e meses, e estações, e anos.

am.B: ልዩ ቀኖችንና ወሮችን፣ ወቅቶችንና ዓመታትን ታከብራላችሁ።
am.R: ልዩ ቀኖችን፣ ወሮችን፣ ወቅቶችንና ዓመታትን በጥንቃቄ ታከብራላችሁ።

decisions.choice: a statement: you are observing
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT punctuates this as a statement, and the Galatians had evidently begun to keep these times. It could also be read as an indignant question; the meaning is much the same.

decisions.choice: days, months, seasons and years: the sacred calendar
decisions.reason: Those troubling the Galatians were urging them to keep the Jewish calendar: sabbaths, new moons, festivals, and perhaps the sabbath years. Paul's general words would fit pagan calendars just as well, which is his point in verse 9: a religion tied to the turning of the heavens belongs to the old order.

decisions.choice: observe carefully
decisions.reason: παρατηρέω means to watch closely, here of keeping religious times with scrupulous care.

decisions.choice: special days
decisions.reason: The days are sacred days, not ordinary ones; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: mnazingatia (L); mnaadhimisha (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to watch closely (m3). Literal says "kuzingatia" (to heed carefully); Balanced and Readable say "kuadhimisha" (to keep a festival), since the days are sacred ones (m2).

source.text: φοβοῦμαι ὑμᾶς μή πως εἰκῇ κεκοπίακα εἰς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: I fear for you lest somehow in vain I have labored for you.

en.L: I fear for you, that somehow I have labored for you in vain.
en.B: I am afraid for you. I fear that the work I did for you may have been wasted.
en.R: I am worried about you. I am afraid that all my hard work for you has been for nothing.

es.L: Temo por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no sea que de algún modo me haya esforzado en vano por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Tengo miedo por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Temo que el trabajo que hice por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se haya perdido.
es.R: Estoy preocupado por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Tengo miedo de que todo mi esfuerzo por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no haya servido para nada.

sw.L: Ninaogopa kwa ajili yenu, huenda kwa namna fulani nimetaabika bure kwa ajili yenu.
sw.B: Nina wasiwasi kwa ajili yenu. Ninaogopa kwamba kazi niliyoifanya kwa ajili yenu huenda imepotea bure.
sw.R: Ninawahangaikia sana. Ninaogopa kwamba bidii yangu yote kwa ajili yenu imekuwa bure.

fr.L: Je crains à votre sujet d’avoir peut-être peiné pour vous en vain.
fr.B: J’ai peur pour vous. Je crains que le travail que j’ai fait pour vous n’ait été perdu.
fr.R: Je suis inquiet pour vous. J’ai peur que tout mon dur travail pour vous n’ait servi à rien.

ko.L: 나는 여러분을 위해 수고한 것이 혹시 헛되지 않았을까 하여 여러분 때문에 두렵습니다.
ko.B: 나는 여러분이 걱정됩니다. 내가 여러분을 위해 수고한 것이 헛일이 되지 않았을까 두렵습니다.
ko.R: 나는 여러분이 걱정됩니다. 내가 여러분을 위해 애써 일한 것이 모두 헛수고가 되었을까 봐 두렵습니다.

vi.L: Tôi lo sợ cho anh chị em, e rằng tôi đã lao nhọc vì anh chị em cách luống công.
vi.B: Tôi lo sợ cho anh chị em. Tôi sợ rằng công khó tôi đã làm cho anh chị em có thể đã trở nên uổng phí.
vi.R: Tôi lo cho anh chị em. Tôi sợ rằng mọi công khó của tôi vì anh chị em đều đã thành vô ích.

pt.L: Temo por vocês, que de algum modo eu tenha trabalhado em vão por vocês.
pt.B: Tenho medo por vocês. Temo que o trabalho que fiz por vocês tenha sido desperdiçado.
pt.R: Estou preocupado com vocês. Tenho medo de que todo o meu trabalho duro por vocês tenha sido à toa.

am.L: ምናልባት ስለ እናንተ በከንቱ ደክሜ እንደ ሆነ እፈራላችኋለሁ።
am.B: እፈራላችኋለሁ፤ ለእናንተ የደከምኩት ድካም ከንቱ ሆኖ ይሆናል ብዬ እሰጋለሁ።
am.R: ስለ እናንተ እጨነቃለሁ። ለእናንተ የደከምኩት ድካም ሁሉ ከንቱ ሆኖ ይሆን ብዬ እፈራለሁ።

decisions.choice: a fear that the harm may already be done
decisions.reason: After a verb of fearing, the perfect tense says Paul fears something may already have happened: that his work among them has already come to nothing.

decisions.choice: labored: worked hard to the point of weariness
decisions.reason: κοπιάω is Paul's word for the hard work of his mission (1 Corinthians 15:10; Philippians 2:16).

source.text: Γίνεσθε ὡς ἐγώ, ὅτι κἀγὼ ὡς ὑμεῖς, ἀδελφοί, δέομαι ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Become as I, because I also as you, brothers, I beg you.

en.L: Become as I [am], because I also [became] as you [were], {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I beg you.
en.B: Be as I am, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I beg you, since I made myself as you were.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, please, be like me. After all, I became like you.

es.L: {{plural_you:Lleguen|Llegad}} a ser como yo, porque yo también [me hice] como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:les|os}} ruego.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como yo soy, hermanos, {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} ruego, ya que yo me hice como {{plural_you:ustedes eran|vosotros erais}}.
es.R: Hermanos, por favor, {{plural_you:sean|sed}} como yo. Al fin y al cabo, yo me hice como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Kuweni kama mimi, kwa sababu mimi pia [nilijifanya] kama ninyi, ndugu, nawasihi.
sw.B: Kuweni kama nilivyo mimi, ndugu, nawasihi, kwa kuwa nami nilijifanya kama mlivyokuwa ninyi.
sw.R: Ndugu, tafadhali, kuweni kama mimi. Kumbukeni, mimi nilijifanya kama ninyi.

fr.L: Devenez comme moi, car moi aussi [je suis devenu] comme vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je vous [en] prie.
fr.B: Soyez comme moi, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, je vous en prie, puisque je me suis fait comme vous.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, je vous en prie, soyez comme moi. Après tout, moi, je suis devenu comme vous.

ko.L: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 내가 여러분에게 간청합니다. 나처럼 되십시오. 나도 여러분처럼 [되었기] 때문입니다.
ko.B: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 간청합니다. 나처럼 되십시오. 나도 여러분처럼 되었습니다.
ko.R: {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 부탁합니다. 나처럼 되십시오. 나도 여러분처럼 되지 않았습니까?

vi.L: Hãy trở nên như tôi, vì tôi cũng [đã trở nên] như anh chị em, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, tôi nài xin anh chị em.
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, tôi nài xin anh chị em hãy trở nên như tôi, vì tôi đã trở nên như anh chị em.
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}}, tôi xin anh chị em hãy trở nên giống như tôi. Vì chính tôi đã trở nên giống như anh chị em.

pt.L: Tornem-se como eu [sou], porque eu também [me tornei] como vocês [eram], {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, eu lhes peço.
pt.B: Sejam como eu sou, {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, eu lhes peço, pois eu me fiz como vocês eram.
pt.R: {{gender:Irmãos e irmãs|Irmãos}}, por favor, sejam como eu. Afinal, eu me tornei como vocês.

am.L: እንደ እኔ ሁኑ፤ እኔ ደግሞ እንደ እናንተ [ሆኛለሁና]፤ {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ሆይ፣ እለምናችኋለሁ።
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞችና እኅቶች|ወንድሞች}} ሆይ፣ እለምናችኋለሁ፤ እኔ እንደ እናንተ ሆኛለሁና እናንተም እንደ እኔ ሁኑ።

decisions.choice: become as I am, because I became as you were: free from the law
alternatives: become as I am, because I am as you are
decisions.reason: The verbs must be supplied. Paul, a Jew, lived like a Gentile among the Galatians, not relying on the law (2:14; 1 Corinthians 9:21). He now asks them to be like him, free from the law, and not to take it up. The second clause can also be read "I am as you are", with the same point.

decisions.choice: "brothers, I beg you" ends the appeal
alternatives: it begins what follows: "Brothers, I beg you: you did me no wrong"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT closes the sentence after "I beg you". The words may instead introduce what comes next; the warmth of the appeal is the same either way.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is speaking to the whole church; the inclusive default spells that out.

decisions.choice: I am (L, B); I became (L, R), I made myself (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out both verbs (m1).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Paul's letters, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, ... 간청합니다" placed first
alternatives: the address and the plea at the end, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: Korean puts an address at the start of what is said to the person addressed; moving "brothers and sisters, I beg you" to the front keeps the appeal in one sentence and loses nothing the Greek says.

en.L: In nothing did you wrong me.
en.R: When I was with you, you did nothing wrong to me.

es.R: Cuando estuve con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no me {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} nada malo.

sw.R: Nilipokuwa pamoja nanyi, hamkunitendea jambo lolote baya.

fr.L: En rien vous ne m’avez fait de tort.
fr.B: Vous ne m’avez fait aucun tort.
fr.R: Quand j’étais avec vous, vous ne m’avez fait aucun mal.

ko.L: 여러분은 나에게 아무 잘못도 하지 않았습니다.
ko.R: 내가 여러분과 함께 있었을 때, 여러분은 나에게 아무 잘못도 하지 않았습니다.

alternatives: you have done me no wrong now
decisions.reason: The past tense looks back to his first stay with them, described in verses 13-14. Paul is not nursing a personal grievance; the issue between them is the gospel.

decisions.choice: When I was with you
decisions.reason: Readable says which time Paul means (m1).

source.text: οἴδατε δὲ ὅτι δι’ ἀσθένειαν τῆς σαρκὸς εὐηγγελισάμην ὑμῖν τὸ πρότερον, καὶ τὸν πειρασμὸν ὑμῶν ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου οὐκ ἐξουθενήσατε οὐδὲ ἐξεπτύσατε, ἀλλὰ ὡς ἄγγελον θεοῦ ἐδέξασθέ με, ὡς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: And you know that because of weakness of the flesh I proclaimed the gospel to you the former [time], \v 14 and the trial of you in the flesh of me not you despised nor you spat out, but as an angel of God you received me, as Christ Jesus.

en.L: And you know that because of a weakness of the flesh I preached the gospel to you the first time, \v 14 and your trial in my flesh you did not despise or spit out, but you received me as an angel of God, as {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus.
en.B: You know that I preached the gospel to you the first time because of a weakness of the flesh. \v 14 And though my flesh was a trial to you, you did not scorn me or spit in disgust. No, you received me like an angel of God, like {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
en.R: You know that the first time I told you the good news, it was because I was sick. \v 14 My illness was hard for you to bear, but you did not look down on me or turn away from me in disgust. You treated me like an angel sent from God, even like {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

es.B: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que la primera vez {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncié el evangelio a causa de una debilidad física. \v 14 Y aunque mi estado físico fue una prueba para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no me {{plural_you:despreciaron|despreciasteis}} ni {{plural_you:escupieron|escupisteis}} con asco. Al contrario, me {{plural_you:recibieron|recibisteis}} como a un ángel de Dios, como {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} en persona.
es.R: {{plural_you:Saben|Sabéis}} que la primera vez que {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncié la buena noticia fue porque estaba enfermo. \v 14 Mi enfermedad fue difícil de soportar para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero no me {{plural_you:despreciaron|despreciasteis}} ni me {{plural_you:rechazaron|rechazasteis}} con asco. Me {{plural_you:trataron|tratasteis}} como a un ángel enviado por Dios, y hasta como {{christos:a Cristo Jesús|al Mesías Jesús}} en persona.

sw.L: Nanyi mnajua kwamba kutokana na udhaifu wa mwili niliwahubiria Injili mara ya kwanza, \v 14 na jaribio lenu katika mwili wangu hamkulibeza wala hamkulitemea mate, bali mlinikaribisha kama malaika wa Mungu, kama {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu.
sw.B: Mnajua kwamba mara ya kwanza niliwahubiria Injili kwa sababu ya udhaifu wa mwili. \v 14 Na ingawa hali ya mwili wangu ilikuwa jaribio kwenu, hamkunidharau wala kunitemea mate kwa kuchukizwa. Badala yake, mlinikaribisha kana kwamba ni malaika wa Mungu, hata kana kwamba ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.

Mlinitendea kama malaika aliyetumwa na Mungu, hata kama {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.

fr.L: Et vous savez que c’est à cause d’une faiblesse de la chair que je vous ai annoncé l’Évangile la première fois, \v 14 et votre épreuve dans ma chair, vous ne l’avez ni méprisée ni repoussée en crachant, mais vous m’avez accueilli comme un ange de Dieu, comme {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} Jésus.
fr.B: Vous savez que c’est à cause d’une faiblesse de la chair que je vous ai annoncé l’Évangile la première fois. \v 14 Et bien que ma chair ait été pour vous une épreuve, vous ne m’avez pas méprisé, vous n’avez pas craché de dégoût. Au contraire, vous m’avez accueilli comme un ange de Dieu, comme le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}.
fr.R: Vous savez que, la première fois que je vous ai annoncé la bonne nouvelle, c’était parce que j’étais malade. \v 14 Ma maladie était difficile à supporter pour vous, mais vous ne m’avez pas regardé de haut, et vous ne vous êtes pas détournés de moi avec dégoût. Vous m’avez reçu comme un ange envoyé par Dieu, et même comme le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}.

ko.L: 여러분이 알다시피, 내가 처음에 여러분에게 복음을 전한 것은 육신의 약함 때문이었습니다. \v 14 그리고 여러분은 내 육신에 있는 여러분의 시험거리를 업신여기거나 침을 뱉지 않고, 나를 하나님의 천사처럼, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수처럼 맞아들였습니다.
ko.B: 여러분도 알다시피, 내가 처음에 여러분에게 복음을 전하게 된 것은 몸이 약해졌기 때문이었습니다. \v 14 내 몸의 형편이 여러분에게 시험거리가 되었는데도, 여러분은 나를 멸시하거나 역겨워하며 침을 뱉지 않았습니다. 오히려 나를 하나님의 천사처럼, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 그분처럼 맞아 주었습니다.
ko.R: 여러분도 알다시피, 내가 처음 여러분에게 기쁜 소식을 전한 것은 내가 병이 들었기 때문이었습니다. \v 14 내 병은 여러분에게 견디기 힘든 것이었지만, 여러분은 나를 업신여기거나 역겨워하며 외면하지 않았습니다. 오히려 하나님께서 보내신 천사처럼, 아니 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수 그분처럼 나를 대해 주었습니다.

vi.L: Và anh chị em biết rằng vì sự yếu đuối của xác thịt mà tôi đã rao giảng Tin Lành cho anh chị em lần đầu, \v 14 và sự thử thách của anh chị em nơi xác thịt tôi, anh chị em đã không khinh dể cũng không nhổ bỏ, nhưng đã tiếp đón tôi như một thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời, như {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu.
vi.B: Anh chị em biết rằng lần đầu tôi rao giảng Tin Lành cho anh chị em là vì thân thể tôi yếu đau. \v 14 Dù thân thể tôi là một sự thử thách đối với anh chị em, anh chị em đã không khinh dể tôi, cũng không nhổ nước bọt ghê tởm. Trái lại, anh chị em đã tiếp đón tôi như một thiên sứ của Đức Chúa Trời, như chính Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Anh chị em biết rằng lần đầu tiên tôi nói Tin Lành cho anh chị em là vì tôi bị bệnh. \v 14 Bệnh tật của tôi là điều khó chịu cho anh chị em, nhưng anh chị em đã không coi thường tôi hay ghê tởm mà xa lánh tôi. Anh chị em đã đối xử với tôi như một thiên sứ Đức Chúa Trời sai đến, thậm chí như chính Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.

pt.L: E vocês sabem que foi por causa de uma fraqueza da carne que eu lhes anunciei o evangelho da primeira vez, \v 14 e a provação de vocês na minha carne vocês não desprezaram nem cuspiram, mas me receberam como um anjo de Deus, como {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} Jesus.
pt.B: Vocês sabem que foi por causa de uma fraqueza da carne que eu lhes anunciei o evangelho da primeira vez. \v 14 E, embora a minha carne fosse uma provação para vocês, vocês não me desprezaram nem cuspiram com nojo. Pelo contrário, vocês me receberam como um anjo de Deus, como {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}} Jesus em pessoa.
